statement: Two trains on parallel tracks travel towards each other, one 150 m long at 20 metres per second and the other 100 m long at 30 metres per second. How many seconds pass from the moment their fronts meet until their rear ends pass each other?

choices.misconception: I used only the length of the shorter train, as if the longer one were a single point.
I used only the length of the longer train, as if the shorter one were a single point.
I used the combined length of 250 m but only one train's speed, 20 metres per second, as if the other train stood still.
I subtracted the speeds, as if the trains travelled in the same direction, instead of adding them.

hints: Imagine sitting in one train: how fast does the other seem to move?
Relative to one train, the other approaches at the sum of their speeds. From fronts meeting to rear ends passing, it must cover the lengths of both trains.
The relative speed is $20 + 30 = 50$ m/s and the distance to cover is $150 + 100 = 250$ m.

solutions.reliable: Watch from the first train. The second train comes past at $20 + 30 = 50$ m/s. When the fronts meet, the rear of the second train is 100 m behind its front, and it must travel until it reaches the rear of the first train, 150 m further, so 250 m in all. Time: $250 \div 50 = 5$ seconds. The transferable idea: for two moving objects, switch to one object's point of view, where speeds add (towards) or subtract (same way), and count every length that has to be covered.

whyOnTest: Passing trains test relative speed and the full distance to be covered; each trap drops one train's length or one train's speed.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
